 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 08.07.2021 in Claim Case No.945/2018 by 26th Additional Member of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore claiming further compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

[2] A Claim Case was preferred by the appellants before the Tribunal claiming Rs.65,00,000/-
regarding death of Mohammad Aasif on 14.10.2017 by Bus bearing registration No.MP-09-F.A.4103 at about 08:00 pm at A.B.Road near Shamshan Ghat submitting that the deceased was aged about 24 years and he was earning Rs.20,000/- pm from private job and contribution in the grocery shop owned by his father.
The Bus bearing registration No.MP-09-F.A.4103 was driven by respondent No.2, owned by respondent No.3 and insured with the respondent No.1/Insurance Company.

[3] The Claim Case was not contested by the respondent No.2 and 3 but contested by the respondent No.1/Insurance Company.
[4] After framing the issues and recording the evidence, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.10,55,000/- vide impugned award dated 08.07.2021.
[5] This Misc. Appeal has been preferred on the ground that income of the deceased has been assessed on lower side that to 25 days in month whereas the appellants examined Chandar Singh who proved that the deceased was working as Supervisor through salary certificate Ex.P/10 which Mohammad Rafiq vs National Insurance Company Ltd. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116898099/
1 clearly established that the monthly salary of the deceased of Rs.15,500/-.
Accordingly, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the income of the appellant of Rs.15000/- with interest of Rs.9%.
[6] The only issue in this case is that whether the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased.

[7] The Tribunal has discussed in para 15 to 17 of the award and discarded the Ex.P/10 to Ex.P/20 adduced to prove the income of the deceased the fact Supervisor (Purchaser and Production) in Juned Engineering, Ydyog Nagar, Nemawar Road, Indore.
The educational qualification are not on record.

Formal technical education is also not on record but pass book (Ex.P/18) of Bank account of deceased maintained in Baroda Bank contains the entries of transfer of amounting Rs.10,000/- on 15.07.2017 and Rs.10,000/- on 29.09.2017 from Juned Engineering and debit entries of Rs.3,000/-
and Rs.5,000/- disclosed that the deceased was engaged with the Juned Engineering with some capacity.

The Income Tax return (Ex.P/13) for the assessment year 2017-18 of Juned Engineering dated 22.09.2017 mentioned the gross total amount of Rs.4,27,646/- in which the deceased is said to be engaged for work.

Accordingly, re-appreciation of the evidence regarding the income of the deceased, the findings of the Tribunal that the deceased was only unskilled labour entitled for 25 working days in a month is not based on the proper appreciation of evidence.
Md. Asif was studied 5th class.

His association with Juned Engineering shows that he was earning as semi skilled person,
accordingly, his per month income is assessed as Rs.7982/- per annum.

On addition of 40% of future prospects, it comes Rs.11,095/- per month and on deduction of personal expenses, it comes Rs.66,570/- per annum, applying multiple of 18, total amount comes Rs.11,98,260/- in the head of loss of dependency.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.9,45,000/- so enhancement of Rs.2,53,260/- is made out with interest of 8% per annum from the date of filing of application i.e.28.02.2018.
The other heads have properly been awarded [8] Zareen Khan/ appellant No.3 is sister and she is not entitled for consortium.
In view of above, Misc. Appeal is allowed in part.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE Praveen Mohammad Rafiq vs National Insurance Company Ltd. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116898099/
